summary: Herbert Mills Birdwood studied at the University of Edinburgh and Peterhouse (circa 1854–1858). He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1858 to 1897.

An indologist and philosopher, Randle studied at Dulwich College, Hertford College, and Oxford (D.Phil. ~1922–1926). He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad, and served as Assistant Librarian and Librarian at the India Office.

Linguist Herbert Petersson earned his Ph.D. at Lund University under Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg, also studying at Rostock, Münster, and Copenhagen. At Lund, he served as Docent from 1911 and ordinary professor of Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European linguistics from 1923.

Herbert Pierrepont Houghton was an indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst College, Princeton, and Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. ~1903–1907). He served as president of Waynesburg University and later as Professor of Classics at Carleton College (1923–1950).
Herbert Schneider was a philosopher who studied at the City University of New York and Columbia University. He held an academic post at Columbia University from circa 1918 to 1957.
Herbert Tower Sorley worked in Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Aberdeen (~1910–1914) and a D.Litt. from the University of Sindh.

Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Munich and Vienna, he held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University before serving as department head at the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert W. Duda was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1932–1936), University of Breslau (~1936–1941), and University of Vienna (~1948–1970).

A scholar of linguistics, Herbert Weir Smyth studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held positions at Williams, Johns Hopkins, and Bryn Mawr before serving as Eliot Professor of Greek Literature at Harvard University from 1902 to 1925.

An indologist and linguist, Magoun studied at Grinnell and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught Greek at Colorado, Oberlin, and Redfield colleges, and served as president of the Massachusetts College of Osteopathy (1921–1926).
Herbert Zachert was a scholar of Japanology who studied under Karl Florenz. He held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1941–1945) and the University of Bonn (~1960–1977).

Herman Almkvist worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala, Paris, Leipzig, and the Collège de France, and was a professor of comparative linguistics and later Semitic languages at Uppsala University.
Indologist Herman Eildert Buiskool completed his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam under Barend Faddegon (~1928–1934). He later served as a conservator at Leiden University from 1936 to 1938.
Herman Frederik Eelsingh was an indologist who studied at Utrecht University under doctoral supervisor Willem Caland, completing his Ph.D. circa 1904–1908.

Herman Kellgren was an indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. at the University of Helsinki. After studying with Franz Bopp, Eugène Burnouf, and others, he became Docent of Sanskrit at Helsinki in 1854.
Herman Neubronner van der Tuuk was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Groningen (~1840–1843) and Leiden University (~1843–1846).

Linguist Hermann Ammann studied at Freiburg and Heidelberg under Rudolf Thurneysen. After working at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and lecturing at Freiburg, he was appointed ordinary professor of Indo-European and general linguistics at the University of Innsbruck in 1928.

Beckh studied at Stiftung Maximilianeum, Kiel, and Humboldt University under Georg Huth and Richard Pischel. Active in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he was PD at Humboldt University and taught at the Priesterseminar der Christengemeinschaft Stuttgart.

Hermann Berger was an indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Munich under Helmut Hoffmann. He held posts at the University of Munich and Sanskrit College and University, and was Director at Heidelberg University (1964–1993).

Hermann Beythan, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1895–1901) and under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai. He was Lecturer in Tamil at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1933–1945).
